rationale: The assistant correctly identified the drying heater / thermostat / thermal cut-out circuit as the leading cause, kept all instructions safe ('switched off and unplugged', 'Do not dismantle the machine or test mains components yourself'), and escalated to an engineer appropriately without naming parts. It never asked the key history question about an interrupted or overloaded drying cycle, nor requested the full model number, and it repeated the pump-filter and hose checks across all three turns even after the customer reported a stone-cold drum and water trickling, which made those checks low-yield. Calibration was honest ('remains the more likely cause') and nothing was fabricated, so the homeowner is reasonably well served, though less efficiently than she could have been.
